findings.name: ledger

diagnosis.summary: Two independent faults in namespace ledger. findings.name: report-worker
findings.root_cause: report-worker container exits with code 137 (OOMKilled) every ~25s because its memory limit is only 32Mi; the process (sh + tail /dev/zero 'warming report cache') exceeds it, so no application error ever appears in logs — the kernel kills it before any output.
findings.fix: Raise the container's memory limit above observed usage (e.g. set limits.memory to at least 128Mi and requests to match actual working set), or remove the unbounded 'tail /dev/zero' warm-up that drives memory past the 32Mi cap.

diagnosis.summary: report-worker in namespace reports crash-loops: pod restarts 3x with exit code 137 / reason OOMKilled (BackOff event). The Deployment sets a 32Mi memory limit while the container command runs an unbounded 'tail /dev/zero' warm-up, so the kernel OOM-kills it within seconds of each start — which is why logs show no application error. Root cause is the undersized memory limit on the report-worker Deployment; fix by raising limits.memory (and/or fixing the warm-up command).

findings.name: pricing-api
findings.root_cause: Calls to pricing-api fail with connection refused because the Service forwards traffic to targetPort 8080 while the pricing-api container only listens on containerPort 80; the pod itself is healthy and ready.
findings.fix: Change the pricing-api Service targetPort from 8080 to 80 (or make the app listen on 8080) so it matches the container's actual listening port.

diagnosis.summary: pricing-api pods are Running/Ready (nginx listening on containerPort 80), but the pricing-api Service maps port 80 -> targetPort 8080, which nothing in the pod listens on. Traffic to the Service therefore hits a closed port and fails with connection refused. Fix: set the Service targetPort to 80 (or run the app on 8080).

findings.name: team-quota
findings.root_cause: Scaling renderer to 5 replicas fails because namespace quota team-quota limits pods to 2; the ReplicaSet's pod creation is rejected with 'exceeded quota: team-quota, requested: pods=1, used: pods=2, limited: pods=2', so only 2 of 5 replicas run.
findings.fix: Raise team-quota hard.pods from 2 to at least 5 (or otherwise accommodate the desired replica count) in namespace batch.

diagnosis.summary: renderer scaled to 5 but only 2/5 running: ResourceQuota team-quota in batch caps pods at 2 (used 2/2), so the ReplicaSet's FailedCreate events show 'exceeded quota'. Root cause is the quota, not the workload. Fix: raise team-quota hard.pods to >=5.

findings.name: web
findings.root_cause: Readiness probe of deployment web does HTTP GET on port 8081, but the nginx:1.29-alpine container runs its default config and listens on port 80; every probe gets 'connection refused', so the pod stays NotReady (0/1) and the deployment reports no availability.
findings.fix: Change the readiness probe in deployment web to target port 80 (or set nginx to listen on 8081 via a custom server block), then the pod will become Ready.

diagnosis.summary: web/web is 0/1 because its readiness probe (httpGet / on port 8081) can never succeed: the stock nginx:1.29-alpine container listens on port 80 by default, so probes get 'connection refused' (event Unhealthy x25). The container itself is healthy per logs. Root cause is the wrong probe port in the Deployment spec; fix it to port 80 (or make nginx listen on 8081). No service exists in this namespace, so once Ready the deployment will be available."

findings.name: search-web
findings.root_cause: search-web's liveness probe execs a busy-loop (i up to 300000) before its wget health check; under the 10m CPU limit that loop takes far longer than timeoutSeconds=1, so the probe times out, kubelet kills the healthy container (exit code 0, no app errors), producing CrashLoopBackOff.
findings.fix: Fix the liveness probe in Deployment search-web: remove the busy-loop from the exec command (just run the wget health check) and/or raise timeoutSeconds above ~5s; consider raising the 10m CPU limit as well.

diagnosis.summary: search-web crash-loops with exit code 0 and no app log errors because its liveness probe is broken: the exec probe runs a 300k-iteration busy-loop before the wget check, which cannot finish within timeoutSeconds=1 (worse under the 10m CPU limit). Kubelet marks it Unhealthy and restarts the healthy container every few minutes (events: 'Liveness probe failed: command timed out', 'failed liveness probe, will be restarted'). Fix the probe command/timeout in the Deployment.

findings.name: reporting-api

findings.fix: Lower reporting-api container requests to cpu 10m, memory 8Mi (well above p95 usage of 0m/3Mi); keep an eye on it after the change.

diagnosis.summary: Rightsize audit of analytics: one material over-provisioned workload — reporting-api (300m/256Mi requested vs ~0m/3Mi used, ~$7.69/mo idle; recommend 10m/8Mi). cache is idle too but its request is tiny (~$0.25/mo), not worth changing. ingest-worker NOT flagged: pinned at its 50m CPU limit (at_limit_share=1.0), i.e. throttled, not over-provisioned. findings.fix: Point checkout-web's trust volume at the internal-ca ConfigMap (ca.crt of 'Internal Services CA 2026') instead of legacy-ca, or append the new CA to the bundle it mounts, then restart the deployment.

diagnosis.summary: payments-api is NOT down: pod Running/Ready, Service has a ready endpoint. Fix: trust the internal-ca CA in checkout-web.
